title: Pods stuck in Pending after node drain
symptom: Workloads would not schedule following a maintenance drain. Events showed insufficient cpu on remaining nodes.
root_cause: The drained node was never uncordoned, so the scheduler had two nodes for three replicas' requests.
resolution: Uncordoned the node and added a PodDisruptionBudget so future drains block rather than silently under-provision.

title: CrashLoopBackOff after a config change
symptom: A deployment entered CrashLoopBackOff immediately after a routine ConfigMap edit.
root_cause: The ConfigMap was mounted with subPath, which does not hot-reload, and the new key was malformed. The pod read a truncated file on restart.
resolution: Fixed the key and moved off subPath so the projection updates in place.

title: OOMKilled under modest load
symptom: Containers were OOMKilled well below the traffic we expected to handle.
root_cause: The JVM sized its heap from the node's memory, not the cgroup limit, so it believed it had far more than the 1Gi limit allowed.
resolution: Set an explicit max heap and aligned requests with limits.

title: Intermittent 503s through the router
symptom: Clients saw sporadic 503s with no corresponding application errors.
root_cause: Readiness probes were slower than the termination grace period, so the router kept endpoints that were already shutting down.
resolution: Lengthened the grace period and added a preStop sleep so endpoints drain before the process exits.

title: DNS resolution failures inside pods
symptom: Applications intermittently failed to resolve in-cluster service names.
root_cause: CoreDNS was CPU-throttled at peak and queries timed out before the second nameserver was tried.
resolution: Raised the CoreDNS CPU limit and lowered ndots to cut lookup volume.

title: gRPC calls fail through the ingress
symptom: A gRPC service worked in-cluster but every call failed through the Route.
root_cause: The Route used edge termination, which does not support HTTP/2, so the connection was downgraded to HTTP/1.1 and gRPC could not negotiate.
resolution: Switched the Route to passthrough and terminated TLS at the workload.

title: Long-running requests cut at 30 seconds
symptom: Streaming responses were severed at almost exactly 30s with no application error.
root_cause: The default HAProxy timeout server is 30s; the Route was edge-terminated so it applied, rather than the 1h tunnel timeout a passthrough Route gets.
resolution: Raised the route timeout annotation and moved the streaming path to passthrough.

title: PersistentVolumeClaim stuck Pending
symptom: A StatefulSet would not start; its PVC never bound.
root_cause: The StorageClass used WaitForFirstConsumer and the pod was unschedulable, so binding could never be triggered. The PVC was a symptom, not the cause.
resolution: Fixed the scheduling constraint; the PVC bound immediately.

title: Disk filled by unrotated container logs
symptom: Nodes went NotReady with disk pressure and pods were evicted.
root_cause: A chatty debug logger was left enabled after an investigation and filled the node filesystem.
resolution: Reverted the log level and set container log rotation limits.

title: Data lost after scaling a StatefulSet down
symptom: Scaling a StatefulSet to zero and back lost the indexes it held.
root_cause: persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy defaulted to Delete on scale-down, so the PVCs were reclaimed with the pods.
resolution: Set the retention policy to Retain and restored from backup.

title: TLS handshake fails with wrong version number
symptom: Clients got 'wrong version number' connecting to a service that had just had TLS enabled.
root_cause: The proxy was configured for TLS but its certificate volumes were never mounted, so it was still listening plaintext while the client spoke TLS.
resolution: Corrected the configuration so the certificates are mounted, and restarted the proxy.

title: Certificate expired in production
symptom: All mutual-TLS connections began failing at the same moment across services.
root_cause: A certificate issued outside cert-manager had no renewal automation, and nothing alerted on expiry.
resolution: Reissued via cert-manager and added an expiry alert.

title: Proxy serving a certificate from the retired CA
symptom: After a CA rotation, clients rejected the server certificate although the Secret held the new one.
root_cause: The proxy reads certificates only at startup and mounts the Secret directly, so it kept serving the old material until restarted.
resolution: Restarted the proxy as the final step of the rotation and documented that ordering.

title: Handshake fails only when dialling by IP
symptom: The same service connected fine by hostname and failed by IP address.
root_cause: TLS clients send no SNI for an IP literal, so the proxy's SNI-matched filter chain matched nothing and dropped the connection.
resolution: Addressed the service by DNS name and added the name to the certificate SANs.

title: Operator cannot create resources after upgrade
symptom: An operator's reconcile loop began failing with forbidden errors after a cluster upgrade.
root_cause: A new API version required an RBAC rule the bundled ClusterRole did not carry.
resolution: Added the missing rule and pinned the operator channel.

title: Pods rejected by PodSecurity admission
symptom: Workloads that ran fine previously were rejected on a namespace after relabelling.
root_cause: The namespace moved to the restricted policy and the pods requested capabilities it disallows.
resolution: Added a compliant securityContext rather than relaxing the namespace.

title: Authentication fails for a service account
symptom: A workload could not authenticate to its datastore despite correct credentials.
root_cause: The password Secret was updated but the consuming pod caches credentials at startup and had not been restarted.
resolution: Restarted the workload and moved to a rollout-triggering annotation on the Secret hash.

title: p99 latency collapses under concurrency
symptom: Throughput fell and p99 rose from 180ms to 16s as concurrency increased, with zero errors.
root_cause: The backend was CPU-capped, so additional concurrency queued rather than failed. The system degraded in latency, not correctness.
resolution: Raised CPU limits and added a concurrency ceiling at the client.

title: One replica serving all traffic
symptom: Three replicas were Ready but one carried every request; the others idled.
root_cause: The client held a single long-lived HTTP/2 connection and the load balancer was L4, so it pinned that connection to one pod. Nothing was unhealthy, so nothing alerted.
resolution: Put an L7 proxy in front so individual streams are distributed, and alerted on per-pod traffic share.

title: Slow queries after a large data load
symptom: Query latency tripled after a bulk import.
root_cause: The search index had not finished building, so queries fell back to a slower path.
resolution: Waited for the index to report queryable and added a readiness gate on it.
